clue.text: Queen replacing theatre in time for procession

indicators.note: one thing replacing another means a piece of a word is taken out and a new one put in its place

parts.note: time served in prison is a sentence
NT is the National Theatre in London
QU is a standard abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A monarch takes the place of a play during a ceremonial parade.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the NT in SENTENCE for QU and you get SEQUENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequence is a succession of things following in order, as a procession is a line moving in order.

clue.text: Actor shifting scenery on an …

indicators.note: shifting things moves them around into new positions

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer moves stage scenery, the ellipsis leading on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean Connery was a Scottish film actor, the first screen James Bond.

clue.text: … independent film pursuing question over America's demise

parts.note: QU is short for question
I is the abbreviation for independent
E.T. is Spielberg's film about an alien
the United States

explanation.surface: Following on from the actor, an indie film asks questions about America's decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursuing' puts the film after the question, and in a down clue 'over' places that chunk above US.
explanation.definitionFit: A quietus is release from life, death; the word comes from the Latin for 'at rest'.

clue.text: Key to take note as soon as daughter's settled snugly

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside

parts.note: ESC is the escape key on a keyboard
N is the abbreviation for note
once means as soon as, as in 'once you arrive'
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A girl settles in comfortably the moment a key note is sounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' tempts you towards musical keys A to G; here it is the computer key ESC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensconced describes being established in a comfortable, secure spot, so settled snugly.

clue.text: Copyright a German article about very strong stimulant

parts.note: C as in the copyright symbol
taken as written
ff is fortissimo, very loud or strong in music
eine is a German indefinite article

explanation.surface: Copyright is claimed on a German piece about a powerful drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Caffeine is the stimulant drug in coffee and tea.

clue.text: Visa risk all banks withdrawing after credit crunch

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its edges, so with them withdrawn only the inner letters of each word stay

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters gone
the word with its first and last letters gone

explanation.surface: Banks shy away from card risk in the wake of the financial meltdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Credit crunch' reads as one phrase, but only 'crunch' is the definition; 'credit' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A crunch is a critical moment or emergency, as in 'when it comes to the crunch', which is a crisis.

clue.text: An angler might handle this river fish

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A fisherman deals with a fish from the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a river eel an angler might handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is the winding device on a fishing rod that an angler operates.

clue.text: Fruit ingredients of pavlova must astonish when put on the counter

indicators.note: counter means opposite in direction, as in counter-clockwise, so the letters run backwards
ingredients are what is inside, so the letters are found inside the words that follow

parts.note: letters running across the words

explanation.surface: A dessert recipe insists that a pavlova must wow guests on the kitchen counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' looks like the kitchen worktop; it means contrary direction. A pavlova is a meringue dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a small, loose-skinned citrus fruit, a type of mandarin.

clue.text: Diffident Greek character voiced by 1 down?

indicators.note: voiced by a speaker means as that person pronounces it, here an actor known for slurring S into SH

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, said like 'kye'

explanation.surface: A shy Greek role is played by the famous actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Sean Connery's famously slushy S sound turns the Greek letter's name into this word; the joke depends on his voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shy is a synonym for diffident, lacking confidence and reserved.

clue.text: Looking up a time zone

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means reading from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Checking a time zone.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or district, as a zone is.

clue.text: Cage birds scratching tin sign

indicators.note: to scratch something is to strike it out, so these letters are removed from the word

parts.note: canaries are the classic caged songbirds
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Birds in a cage scratch at a tin notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Showing intense passion, run in race — perhaps as sprint's over

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is placed inside it

parts.note: to fly is to go very fast, as a sprinter does

indicators.note: something that is over another covers it, wrapping around it

parts.note: a race at an athletics meeting is an event
R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: An athlete runs with fierce passion as the sprint finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: the run goes inside the race first, and that whole chunk then sits inside the sprinting word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervently is an adverb meaning with ardour and zeal, the manner of someone showing intense passion.

clue.text: Channel starting with poem by artist inspired by Heathcliff's love — it used to give TV depth

definitions.text: it used to give TV depth

indicators.note: something inspired by another is breathed in by it, so it goes inside

parts.note: Cathy is Heathcliff's beloved in Wuthering Heights
an ode is a lyric poem
RA is a Royal Academician
a tube is a channel or pipe

explanation.surface: A TV channel launches with a poem by an artist moved by a Brontë heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Heathcliff and Cathy are the lovers of Emily Brontë's Wuthering Heights. 'Starting with' puts the inspired chunk before the channel; old televisions were deep boxes because of this part.
explanation.definitionFit: Old televisions used a cathode ray tube, a deep glass tube that made the set bulky front to back.

clue.text: See 12
Corrupt CEO's money essentially seized — revealing promise of more for less

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or perverted, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters

explanation.surface: A crooked chief executive's cash is confiscated, exposing a bargain-style scam.
explanation.definitionFit: An economy-size pack is a large one sold cheaper per unit, the promise of more product for less money.

clue.text: Understands broadcast — fiddle with electronic part of rocket

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to know is to understand
a fiddle is a swindle, a con
E is the usual abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Someone grasps a broadcast about tampering with electronics.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose cone is the pointed front section of a rocket or missile.

clue.text: Penny discovered Tom Jones, a Welsh singer, cycling on board boat

indicators.note: something on board is held within the vessel, so it sits inside the other letters
letters cycling go round like a wheel, so some move from the front to the back

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny

indicators.note: dis-covered means with the covering stripped off, so the outside letters of the word go

parts.note: the word with its outer letters removed
Aled Jones is a Welsh singer, famous as a boy treble

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny spots Tom Jones out cycling, as if the singer were aboard a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom Jones' looks like one singer, but the clue splits it: Tom loses its outsides, and Jones points to Aled Jones, another Welsh singer, famous as a boy treble.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedalo is a small pleasure boat driven by pedals, the kind hired on lakes and beaches.

clue.text: Shame Mars bars supply energy to begin with

indicators.note: read as supple-y, in a pliant way, so the letters bend into a new order
to begin with places this piece at the very start of the answer

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: It is a disgrace that chocolate bars provide our energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars bars are a chocolate bar; 'supply' looks like the verb 'provide' but works as an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: To shame someone is to embarrass or humiliate them.

clue.text: Concentrate — caught on boundary

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written
a verge is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder focuses hard to take a catch at the boundary rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To concentrate in the sense of gathering at a common centre is to converge on one point.

clue.text: Gather together after action — demob happy at last

indicators.note: letters that have seen action have been knocked about and rearranged

parts.note: the letters rearranged

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Soldiers released from service after combat are cheerful at last; 'demob happy' is British slang for elated at leaving the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To embody is to incorporate or unite separate parts into one whole, so to gather them together.

clue.text: Noxious airline fuel spilt next to Bristol's terminal

indicators.note: spilt liquid is scattered about, so these letters land in a new order

parts.note: BA is British Airways
the letters rearranged

indicators.note: a terminal is the end, so only the last letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of the city's name

explanation.surface: Harmful aviation fuel is spilled near Bristol airport's terminal building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminal' tempts you to an airport building; it is the end of Bristol.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleful means menacing or harmful, which is close to noxious, injurious or poisonous.

clue.text: Melancholy men returning hat

parts.note: sombre means gloomy

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: OR is 'other ranks', soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Gloomy men come back wearing a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Copy insubordination — ignoring leader

indicators.note: ignoring the leader means passing over the front letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: sedition is incitement to rebel against authority

explanation.surface: A defiant underling imitates rebellion by ignoring the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy of a book or newspaper is one example of a particular edition, so the words overlap as printing terms.

clue.text: With guidance I naively try and sue American college

indicators.note: guidance steers things into a new course, so these letters are sent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An applicant admits to naively trying, with a counsellor's help, to sue an Ivy League school.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is an Ivy League university in New Haven, Connecticut, and college is a common American word for a university.

clue.text: See 23
Pleasant Mediterranean resort

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the city on the French Riviera

explanation.walkthrough: The same spelling covers an everyday adjective and the French city, pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is a plain synonym of agreeable, and the proper noun names a famous seaside city in southern France.

clue.text: Leading man appearing in the round

indicators.note: appearing in means being found within the words that follow

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: The star actor performs in a theatre in the round.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero is the principal male character in a story or film, its leading man.

clue.text: Pound about right for on-line snack service?

parts.note: to pound is to batter or buffet
CA is circa, Latin for about
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether a pound is fair for an internet snack delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on-line' looks like internet shopping, but the line is a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet car is the carriage on a train where snacks and drinks are sold, a service running along the line.

clue.text: Youngster's prize books removed

definitions.note: the clue's 's is 'is', joining definition and wordplay

indicators.note: removed means taken away, so these letters are cut out of the word

parts.note: booty is plunder or a prize
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.definitionFit: A boy is a male child, a youngster.

clue.text: Occasionally tabloid called out Times's excuse

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

indicators.note: called out means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: times as in multiplication, three by four

explanation.surface: A tabloid now and then shouts out the Times's justification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is the multiplication word 'by', said aloud as BI.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used as an excuse or defence.

clue.text: Cowardly scream "that hurt!"

parts.note: to scream is to yell
ow is the cry of pain

explanation.surface: A timid person shrieks at a minor pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is informal for lacking courage, as in yellow-bellied.

clue.text: Go to cover firebombing — maybe originally ascribed to far right characters

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, so these letters wrap the others
the original, first letter is reassigned to the far right end, rotating the word

parts.note: 'go' is a euphemism for urinating, to pee

explanation.surface: Arsonists' firebombing may be attributed to far-right figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far right' looks political; here it means the far right-hand end of the word, where its original first letter is moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Personae is the plural of persona, a role or character in a play or novel.
